verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission successfully launched on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '6:36 PM / April 1, 2026 Artemis II lifts off Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT.'; R2: 'blasted off from Florida on Wednesday evening... at 6:35 p.m. Eastern time.'; R3: 'lifted off... at 6:35 p.m. EDT'; R5: 'At 6:35 p.m. ET, the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket...'; R6: '6:35 pm ET April 1, 2026Artemis II liftoff!'; R7: 'NASA’s Artemis II mission has officially lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact date, time, location, and successful launch.

verifications.claim: The Space Launch System (SLS) rocket is currently carrying four astronauts—Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen—on a 10-day trip around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'astronauts — commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; R3: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with CSA... Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'Mr. Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen on... 10-day mission'; R5: '10-day mission around the moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm exact crew names, SLS rocket, and 10-day lunar mission post-launch.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission crew is in orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II crew begins first day in space... orbiting the Earth'; R2: 'Orion capsule is taking... into a high-Earth orbit'; R3: 'core stage has successfully separated... transition to upper‑stage operations'; R5: 'Artemis II crew aboard Orion successfully executed an apogee-raise burn, placing the spacecraft into a stable high Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Post-launch updates explicitly state crew is in orbit around Earth.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission spacecraft is performing as expected following successful separation from the rocket.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Core stage separates... successfully separated'; 'Orion separates from interim cryogenic propulsion stage'; R3: 'core stage has successfully separated'; R2: 'The Orion spacecraft separated from the upper stage of the rocket'; R5: 'ascent of Artemis II is progressing perfectly, with all systems... operating nominally'
verifications.reasoning: Sources detail successful separations and nominal performance post-separation.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight to the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago'; R2: 'last time astronauts traveled that far was Apollo 17, in December 1972'; R4: 'first time astronauts return to the vicinity of the moon in more than 50 years'; R5: 'first crewed mission to the moon in over 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm first crewed lunar mission since Apollo 17 in 1972.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is the first to fly beyond low-Earth orbit in over five decades.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first time in 50 years a spacecraft carrying people is traveling far enough'; R2: 'first time astronauts rode... beyond low-Earth orbit since 1972'; R3: 'first crewed deep-space flight in over 50 years'; R4: 'first time in more than 50 years'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state first crewed flight beyond LEO in 50+ years.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission lasts 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day trip around the Moon'; R2: '10-day mission'; R3: 'approximately 10-day Artemis II mission'; R4: '10 days long'; R5: '10-day mission'; R7: '10-day journey'
verifications.reasoning: Overwhelmingly described as 10-day mission; minor variations like 'about nine and a half days' in R1 do not contradict.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is aimed at testing critical systems for future moon landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test their Orion capsule... making sure the ship's communications, navigation, propulsion and life support systems are working properly before heading to the moon'; R2: 'check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey... for docking with lunar landers'; R3: 'test the systems and hardware needed to continue sending astronauts on... missions'; R4: 'test critical systems aboard Orion'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm mission purpose is testing systems for future lunar missions.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission includes three Americans and one Canadian.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'first Black man... first woman... first person... not an American'; R3: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: Crew consistently listed as three NASA (American) astronauts and one Canadian.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is the first crewed flight of the Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA's Artemis II mission has... first with a crew on board'; R3: 'The approximately 10-day Artemis II mission around the Moon is the first crewed flight under NASA’s Artemis campaign'; R5: 'first crewed mission to the moon in over 50 years'; R6: 'first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft'
verifications.reasoning: Sources state Artemis II as first crewed Artemis mission (Artemis I uncrewed).
